obligations.text: When a gate declares `integrity`, a candidate any of whose runs, or any baseline run, exceeds a declared bound or has a count that cannot be established is `unknown` naming that run, with every coverage minimum and clause unevaluated; such a candidate is never `rejected`, never `qualifies` and never ranked.

An integrity count is computed only from documents the selection has verified; a count that is missing, unknown or cannot be derived (no declared scorer for `max_invalid`, a declared scorer without its scores) voids the comparison and is never taken as zero.
A selection gate without `integrity` has the same canonical bytes and identity as today, and `gate select` over it writes the same `rustev.selection/1` bytes, stdout and exit code.

sectionHeadings: 065: Selection gate: run integrity failures void the comparison instead of rejecting (amends 029 and 061)
record.summary: An amendment of approved specs 029 (3.12) and 061 (3.7), for release 0.6.0 (#538), ratified by the owner on 2026-11-06 (A-84). A run with integrity failures (results the evaluator could not score, cases a backend or source failed on) is not a measurement, yet today it can only lower coverage and reject the candidate, which reads as a verdict about the candidate when the run is the problem. This spec adds an optional integrity precondition to `rustev.selection-gate/1`, `integrity: { max_invalid, max_upstream_failures }`, counted per run on each side from documents the selection already verifies. A breach, or a count that cannot be established, voids the comparison: the candidate is `unknown` naming the run, no coverage minimum or clause is evaluated, and so it can never be rejected or qualify on a void run; a baseline run in breach voids every candidate. Gates without the member keep their bytes, identities and results.
record.title: Selection gate: run integrity failures void the comparison instead of rejecting (amends 029 and 061)
